steps.prompt: The librarian asked, “Where is your library card?” Which report sounds right?
steps.a: The librarian asked me where was my library card?
steps.b: The librarian asked me where my library card was.
steps.reveal: B. A reported question isn’t a question any more: it’s a statement about a question. So the words go back to statement order (my library card was), and it ends with a full stop.

cards.title: Yes/no questions: if or whether
cards.text:
“Are you ready?” → She asked if I was ready.
“Can we stay?” → They asked whether they could stay.
cards.note: Add “if” or “whether”, use statement order (I was, they could), shift the verb back, and end with a full stop.

cards.title: Question-word questions
cards.text:
“Where do you live?” → He asked where I lived.
“What time is it?” → Dad asked what time it was.
“Why did you leave?” → She asked why I had left.
cards.note: Keep the question word, then statement order. “Do”, “does” and “did” disappear: the main verb carries the tense.

cards.title: Commands and requests: to + verb
cards.text:
“Sit down.” → The teacher told us to sit down.
“Please help me.” → Mia asked me to help her.
“Don’t touch it!” → Dad told us not to touch it.
cards.note: Use told, asked, ordered, reminded or warned + the person + to + the verb. A “don’t” command becomes “not to”.

cards.title: The most common slips
cards.telling: Coach asked if were we tired? Then he told us run another lap.
cards.showing: Coach asked if we were tired. Then he told us to run another lap.
cards.note: Check three things: statement order, a full stop, and “to” for commands.

prompts: Write one question someone asked you this week, then report it. What changed?
Which is harder to report, a question or a command? Why?
